summary: The root وَكَلَ (wakala) primarily means to rely upon someone, confide in them, or submit oneself to them.
lane: 5 تَوَكَّلَ عَلَيْهِ ذ , and عليه , He relied upon him; (S, Msb;) and confided in him: (Msb:) he submitted himself to him. (K.) -b2- تَوَكَّلَ بِالأَمْرِ He became responsible to him for the management of the affair. (TA.) -b3- تَوَكَّلَ لَهُ بِهِ He became responsible to him for it. (TA.) -b4- تَوَكَّلَ فِى أَمْرٍ He became وَكِيل in an affair. -b5- توكّل بِمَالِ أَحَدٍ He became administrator of one's property.

headwords.def: وَكَلَهُ إِلَى رَأْيِهِ , inf. n. وَكْلٌ and وُكُولٌ, He left him to his opinion, or judgment. (TA.) And وَكَلْتُهُ إِلَى نَفْسِهِ, aor. يَكِلُ, inf. n. وُكُولٌ, [ I left him to himself; ] I did not manage his affair, nor aid him. (Msb.) And كِلْنِى إِلَى كَ َا Leave thou me to manage such a thing. (TA.) وَكَلْتُهُ إِلَى دِينِهِ [ I left him to his religion, not interfering with him therein ]. (S, Msb, K, voce دَيَّنْتُهُ.)

وَكَّلَهُ بِشَىْءٍ He appointed him, or intrusted him, as his commissioned agent, factor, or deputy, with the management, or disposal, of a thing. وَكَّلْتُ بِفُلَانٍ I associated a وَكِيل [or factor, &c.] with such a one. (T in art. بِ.)

تَوَكَّلَ عَلَيْهِ , and عليه, He relied upon him; (S, Msb;) and confided in him: (Msb:) he submitted himself to him. (K.) تَوَكَّلَ بِالأَمْرِ He became responsible to him for the management of the affair. (TA.) تَوَكَّلَ لَهُ بِهِ He became responsible to him for it. (TA.) تَوَكَّلَ فِى أَمْرٍ He became وَكِيل in an affair. توكّل بِمَالِ أَحَدٍ He became administrator of one's property.
He deserted him, or it: i. q. تركته: see two exs. voce سَدِرٌ.
إِوْتَكَلَ see 5. مُتَّكَلٌ is used as an inf. n. of اِتَّكَلَ.
and and An impotent man, (S, K,) who commits his affair to another. (S.)
A witness; syn. شَهِيدٌ. (Jel, ii. 66; and iv. 169.) A commissioned agent; a factor; a deputy.
for دَارُ الوَكَالَةِ, A factory: pl. وَكَائِلُ.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
